questions.stem: A sound wave has a frequency of 500 Hz and travels at 340 m/s in air. What is its wavelength?
questions.explanation: Using λ = v / f = 340 / 500 = 0.68 m. Always check your rearrangement of the wave equation: to find wavelength, divide wave speed by frequency.

questions.stem: What determines the speed of a wave?

options.text: The medium through which it travels

questions.explanation: Wave speed is determined by the properties of the medium through which the wave travels, not by the source. For example, sound travels at about 340 m/s in air but 1500 m/s in water, regardless of the source frequency.
